No, the pedestrian will not prevail. The adjuster's statement was a knowing misstatement of law, but misrepresentation also requires justifiable reliance and resulting damage. The pedestrian rejected the offer, hired an attorney, and recovered $550,000, so they relied on nothing and lost nothing. The adjuster also owed no fiduciary duty to a third-party claimant, since the adjuster was adverse to the pedestrian and not their protector.

CONFIDENCE: 88
